paragraphs: Markets over the past seven days: the eight tracked equity indices moved +1.00% on average, with Nikkei 225 strongest (+7.95%) and Hang Seng weakest (-1.47%). Brent crude changed -2.57% to 100.87. Gold changed -1.21% to 4,136.1001. Bitcoin changed -1.23% to 83,454.1562. The US 10-year yield stands at 5.316%, a relative move of +0.43%. Among the firms tracked, 3i Group (-8.88%) and Deutsche Bank (-6.67%) moved the most.

Deals and capital markets: Germany blocks Chinese acquisition in its largest seaport (FT World). Berlin rejects state-owned Cosco’s takeover of a Hamburg port logistics group ‘on security concerns’ Deals and capital markets: Auditor RSM explores IPO to ward off private equity-backed rivals (FT Home). Accounting firm has been sounding out bankers and revamping internal systems to give itself the option of a stock market flotation Central banks and macro: French central bank chief says ECB intervention not needed to ease bond rout (FT World). Emmanuel Moulin also hit out at ‘Trump-style’ threats against him from the far-left Central banks and macro: French central bank head warns country at risk of being ‘strangled by interest rates’ (FT Markets). Emmanuel Moulin says France can still reassure bond investors despite ‘serious and worrying’ market moves in recent days Geopolitics and trade: International Criminal Court cuts ties with Axa over US sanctions (FT World). Move follows fears that broad US sanctions on the war crimes tribunal would force the insurer to cease doing business with it or face punishment
